about: The course format's step kinds and fields (docs/plus-courses-build-plan.md 6a; web/course/format/README.md). Each kind says which app plays it: yes, no (that app says 'open this lesson on the web'), or unknown (not verified). web/tool/course_check.py fails on a kind or field not listed here. Add a field here when you add it to a lesson, with a line saying what it is.

unitBoss.about: A unit's boss round (docs/boss-round-plan.md in the app's repo): { id, title, steps }, beside the unit's lessons and never in them, so stars, unit opening and the next lesson don't change. id is the unit's number then -boss (3-boss); 2 to 4 sung `play` steps (song steps welcome; no record step, which would leave the round for Sing), checked as a lesson's are, with no keep or thenAndNow. Opens once the unit's challenge has stars, never in a singer's first week; 80% across its steps (notes-weighted) beats it. Web only: an app that doesn't play bosses skips the field.

lessonExtras.about: Lesson fields an app may leave out without breaking the lesson: a lesson that has one still plays, so neither makes it web-only. docs/ux-spec.md says how each is shown.

fact.about: The lesson end's "Did you know?" card: one checked fact, said in one course only. id: a kebab-case name, unique across every course; text and source: words; url: the source's page, a quiet link; distinct: ids of facts in other courses it may share two names or years with, since the check fails on those as one fact told twice. One or two a unit.

keepSong.about: The lesson end offers to keep the finale as a song in Sing, on the device. title: words; takes: [{ step, name }], the sung steps (from 0) whose kept takes become tracks; from: the step whose partner lines (with, in order, named by partners: [words]) and chords (named by chords: words, optional) become tracks too.

learn.about: A headline, up to three cards, a picture; may play an example (listen: an exercise)

try.about: Wait for me: each note plays and waits until it's found; unscored

play.about: Hear it, then sing it back (turn: true), or sing over a drone or chords (turn: false); scored

use.about: Opens a song in Sing; done after 20 seconds sung

record.about: Records a part in Sing; scored on pitch. The song is a template (a free or library song), or a Plus course's own (`courseSong`: songs/<id>.json in the course's folder, a template file whose id is <id>)

wave.about: The trace lane: ride a ribbon (a steered wave, a straight line, a bloom, a free hold, a contour); `keep` saves the first take on the device under a key, and `thenAndNow` shows it beside today's

choose.about: Listen and choose, no mic: tap a clip or a word; `base: flip` lays its clips from the singer's flip note (Yodeling)

selfcheck.about: What we can't hear yet: hear a model, record, compare, answer self-check questions; never scored; its model may name a real singer's clip (`clip`), with `seconds` and a `description` until it's recorded; `base: flip` lays its model from the singer's flip note (Yodeling)

bullseye.about: Echo a note and see where it landed (Perfect your pitch: docs/courses/perfect-pitch.md)

breathhold.about: A held note that ends when you stop (Breath and stamina: docs/courses/breath.md)

play.about: A play, try or learn-listen exercise's fields. Those marked web-only make the step web-only for now.

fields.turn: true: hear it, then sing it back; false: sing over the drone or chords
fields.drone: { step, fadeAfter?, fadeOver? }: a held note under it; with fadeAfter it fades to silence from that many beats after the exercise's start (the listen phase included) over fadeOver beats (4 by default); fadeAfter: beats until it fades out, so do is heard first and the line is then read alone
fields.chords: [{ beat, root, quality, bass }]: chords under it, root in semitones from home
fields.score: how it's starred: hold, or a registered scorer (web/js/lesson-scores.js)
fields.show: vibrato: describe a held note's vibrato after the take
fields.base: flip: steps laid from the singer's flip note (Yodeling); flipKey: the same, moved up to three semitones (or one down) so the tag's home note, two below, is in the line's key (lineKey), else its V, else its IV: a song's yodel tag
fields.lineKey: with base flipKey: the song line's home note, in semitones from the singer's comfortable note (0 by default)
fields.under: { step }: sing over that earlier step's take, this visit. Or layers (Live looping, docs/courses/live-looping.md): { steps: [n | { step, loop }], loop? }: those earlier steps' takes mixed, each first layer loudest and each later one a little quieter; with loop (beats), a layer plays from its take's beat 0 for that many beats, again and again, to the exercise's end (a layer's own loop over the shared one; shorter loops divide the longest). Through a speaker the layers rest during a scored take. keepSong renders each loop out to the song's length.
fields.with: partner lines that sound while you sing (Counterpoint: docs/courses/counterpoint.md 8b)
fields.answer: the notes to sing back when they differ from the call (call and response)
fields.guide: false: no guide notes (a cold start)
fields.droneAfter: with guide: false, the drone comes in this many beats into your turn
fields.window: a lazy scoop's time to arrive, in seconds (Pop and country: docs/courses/pop-country.md)
fields.giveNote: true: a Give me my note button while you sing your turn (not through a speaker); the note is played quietly, once, and never scored (Folk: docs/courses/folk.md)
fields.rules: with score species: contrary (three moves against the first partner), all (every first-species rule), close (four moves in five a step or less, with some real moving) or against (half the moving notes against the tune) for three stars (docs/courses/counterpoint.md 8b)
fields.lights: how your notes are drawn, all still scored: on (the default), fade (the second half faint), changes (only where the chord changes), late (after a beat off) or off (Improvising a harmony: docs/courses/improvising-harmony.md)
fields.keep: an id ("<course>.<name>"): the step's first heard take is kept on this device, never synced, for Then and now
fields.thenAndNow: an id an earlier lesson keeps: after the take, that first take plays beside today's (Then and now, every course's finale)
fields.song: { template, part, phrases, with? }: the notes come from that song's part in those phrases (from 0, every section's in order), loaded with the song so a Plus song's notes stay private; with: others plays the other parts as partner lines. With turn: false the guide sings your line with you, unless guide: false; without others, the song's chords play under you. An exercise has song or notes, never both (a song course, course/songs: docs/song-courses-plan.md)
fields.tuning: true: the ring meter shows while a note of a beat or more is held in the step's chord (its chords, or its drone as the root): how close it is to pure, not just the piano's pitch (js/tuning.js ringReading, ux-spec 5.10c). A view only, never scored; hidden through a speaker.
fields.staff: { names: on | faint | off, look: seconds }: the line drawn on a stave instead of the lane, in the key whose do is the singer's note, the clef from its range; names under the notes in the singer's chosen style (solfege by default), faint, or none; look: seconds it shows still before it runs, counted on the audio clock (Sight-singing: docs/sight-singing-plan.md); count: count-in beats in the time's own beat (0 to 8; 6/8 counts dotted quarters); time: "4/4" | "3/4" | "2/4" | "6/8" (default 4/4; notes stay in quarter-note beats, and a line fills whole bars); rhythm: true also scores when each note starts (pitch 70, timing 30, pitch alone when timing can't be read)
fields.hearFirst: true: "Hear it first" is offered before the take; a take after hearing it is capped just under the top score, and the result says so
fields.keyRange: { down, up }: how far "Not in your range?" may move the key from the line as written, in semitones (whole numbers, 0 to 12); up 0 hides Higher. It applies to the whole lesson, the tightest across its steps; a remembered key is held inside it (First steps to belting: { "down": 4, "up": 0 })
fields.retries: a whole number, 1 to 10: after that many heard takes in a visit, Sing it again, the more-stars offer and the guide take go, and the way on says "Good enough: move on" (First steps to belting: 3)

fields.step: semitones from the learner's comfortable note (do = 0)
fields.vibrato: { hz, cents, after, jitter }: the guide's own vibrato on this note
fields.bend: [[seconds, cents], ...]: the guide's pitch path on this note
fields.style: scoop, fall, slide or cry (Pop and country: docs/courses/pop-country.md)
fields.ring: false: never ring-scored (a chord with no pure tuning, such as a diminished seventh)
fields.cents: a pure-tuning offset for this note (Barbershop)

segment.about: A wave step's target: one segment after another

fields.kind: wave, straight, bloom, free or path
fields.cents: a wave's width, plus or minus
fields.fade: seconds for the ribbon to fade (the ghost wave)
fields.straight: a bloom's straight seconds before the wave
fields.band: a path's ribbon width, plus or minus cents
fields.voice: head: the guide sings this segment in head voice

lessonUnscored: unscored: true makes a lesson practice only: no stars, no XP, no progress or practice record, and its end shows endLine (words) in place of a score; minutes says how long it takes. Every wave target in it is scored: false, and it has no play, record or use step (the cool-down, course/cooldown.json).
lessonVariants: variants: { "<experiment id>-<arm>": { steps, minutes? } }: in an A/B test (docs/experiments.md), a device drawn into that arm gets these steps in place of the lesson's; everything else (id, title, findsHome) stays the lesson's, and arm a or a device not drawn gets the lesson as written. The id must be in course/format/experiments.json. Removing the losing arm is deleting the variant, or moving its steps into the lesson.
courseGame: game: optional, game mode's rules for this course (First steps to belting's voice-health review: no game pressure); every field optional, absent = as everywhere. replayXp: false = a lesson already starred pays no XP when sung again (the first finish pays as usual); combo: false = no combo counter, bonus pop-ups or combo bonus XP on its steps; streak: false = its lesson ends show no streak chip and no Streak! burst; meter: "plain" (its only value) = its takes keep the plain bars, never game mode's power-bar or level-meter look. The lesson view applies them as one of the course's lessons opens and drops them as it closes, so every other course keeps everything.
lessonQuiet: quiet: true = game mode's moments off for this lesson (no pop-ups, fanfares, title card or celebration); the arcade look stays. Optional, absent = false (First steps to belting's spiritual line).
courseDailyCap: dailyCap: { minutes }: the course's lessons stop for the day after that many minutes (a whole number, 1 to 60), checked only as a lesson opens and counted only while one of its lessons is open and on screen, kept per day with the account (progress.courses.<id>.capDay); then the rest card (en.json course.dailyCap.*, which names belting: a second capped course needs its own words). First steps to belting: { "minutes": 10 }.
courseParts: parts: { template, choose, default }: the singer picks one of the template's parts (choose, in score order; default when nothing is known; the app suggests one from the singer's range) and the pick is kept per course (progress.courses.<id>.personal.part). Then "part": "yours" in a song spec (exercise.song, listen.song) or a record step sings the pick; a learn step's byPart { <part>: { headline, steps } } and a sung step's textByPart { <part>: words } replace that step's own words for the picked part (whole: every card written out), the step's own words being the default part's. Then and now keeps a first take per part. Learn your part for rehearsal (docs/courses/choir-part-sections-plan.md in the app's repo).
